description: A second `struct` declaring an already-declared type name raises `ol-duplicate-definition` at phase-1 registration, carrying BOTH spans: `source_span` at the later declaration (line 2) and `params.original_span` at the earlier one (line 1), so the message can name the line the learner already used (`spec/error-model.md:126,144-147`). Ruling #833 rule 6 gives redefining YOUR OWN name its own code, leaving `ol-reserved-word` with exactly one meaning. The field lists deliberately DIFFER (`[ x y ]` vs `[ a b ]`) so this fixture cannot pass under a rule that only notices two identical declarations. `check()` reports the identical code, params and spans for this program. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
